summary: Petition under Section 79(1)(c) & (f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 41 and 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 seeking extension of time for submission of land documents under Regulation 5.8(xi)(b) with directions to Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd. to not take any coercive action in the interregnum in relation to connectivity granted to the Petitioners from KurnoolIII Pooling Sub-station on 6.11.2024. Order in Petition No. 862/MP/2025 & IA No.108/IA/2025 Page 1 of 7 _(b) Pass any such other / further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and equitable in the facts and circumstances of the present case.”_ 3. The Petitioners have also sought the following interim relief in the petition: _“(a) Restrain Respondent No. 1 – CTUIL from taking any coercive action against the Petitioners, including revocation of connectivity granted to the Petitioner from KurnoolIII PS on 06.11.2024 and/or encashment of the Connectivity BGs and/or Land BGs submitted by the Petitioners._ _(b) Pass any such other / further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and equitable in the facts and circumstances of the present case.”_ Order in Petition No. 862/MP/2025 & IA No.108/IA/2025 Page 2 of 7 _Provided that for States where State Government issues Government Order for allotment of Land to the Nodal Agency identified for development of Renewable energy in the State, which in turn issues Advance Possession of land to the project developer, such Government Order allotting land to the Nodal Agency accompanied with Advance Possession letter issued in the name of Applicant of Connectivity, shall be considered as a valid document towards Land Use Rights subject to the condition that the said documents shall be submitted for at least 50% of the land required for the capacity for which Connectivity is sought;_ Order in Petition No. 862/MP/2025 & IA No.108/IA/2025 Page 3 of 7 Order in Petition No. 862/MP/2025 & IA No.108/IA/2025 Page 4 of 7 7. The matter was heard on 6.11.2025 and during the hearing learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that the Petitioners have received information that the advance possession for land for solar as well wind capacities of the Projects have been received. After hearing the Petitioners and the CTUIL, the Commission reserved the order in the matter and directed the parties to file a brief note of arguments within three days. 8. The Petitioners have filed their written submissions on 10.11.2025 stating that the Petitioners have received the documents regarding advance possession of land in respect of its wind and solar projects. The relevant portions of the submissions made by the Petitioners in this regard is as follows: details of the progress that has been made with respect to land acquisition for the Projects since 3.11.2025. The Petitioners have also enclosed a copy of the orders bearing Ref. No. E1/LES/(OTH)/33/2025/C.No.577467, Ref. No. E1/ALN/67/2025/C.No.588591 and Ref. No. E1/ALN/68/2025/C.No.588592 issued by the District Collector of Y.S.R. Kadapa District, to the Tahsildar of the concerned Mandals directing them to take immediate steps for collection of lease rent from the NREDCAP, the Nodal Agency and the Petitioners in respect of the Government land specified in the orders, for which advance possession Orders are issued. The Order in Petition No. 862/MP/2025 & IA No.108/IA/2025 Page 5 of 7 10. We have considered the submissions made by the Petitioners after the hearing on 6.11.2025. As stated earlier in this order, the order was reserved in the matter after hearing the parties on 6.11.2025, and the parties were directed to file note of arguments within three days. However, the Petitioners have filed an affidavit dated 10.11.2025 stating that the Petitioners are in advance possession of the land and have also submitted documents, as mentioned above to claim that they are in advance possession of the land required for execution of the Project. Considering the fact that the last date to furnish the land documents is 6.11.2025 and the learned counsel for the Petitioner informed on 6.11.2025 that it has received the required documents dated 6.11.2025, which have been filed on 10.11.2025, we are of the view that the documents furnished by the Petitioner are required to be vetted by CTUIL to see whether they meet the requirements of the 2022 GNA Regulations. Taking into consideration the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioners during the hearing on 6.11.2025 that the Petitioners have received advance possession of the land required for solar and wind capacities of the Project and the submissions and the documents filed by the Petitioners subsequently, we take the affidavit dated 10.11.2025 and the “Brief Submissions of the Petitioners” filed by the Petitioners on record. 11. The CTUIL is directed to verify the documents submitted by the Petitioners, within 15 days of issue of this order, to see whether the documents submitted by the Petitioners are in accordance with the 2022 GNA Regulations and in case the Order in Petition No. 862/MP/2025 & IA No.108/IA/2025 Page 6 of 7 documents are not in order, take suitable action as per the provisions of the 2022 GNA
